value: Calls the toll from the spit and writes each boat on a slate, one column for Thorn and one for Hissmir.
Takes the fares under the stage shelter; no canoe leaves with a passenger who has not eaten.
Airs the reed mattresses in the long house every dry morning.
Gathers herbs on the cove shore and sorts the bundles by smell.
Holds that trodh must be eaten alive.
Hums to the stroke while poling the raft along the channel.
Copper caps on both horns, polished every dusk.
Has the best bunk in the crews' house, won at Shells and Stones.
The shrine at the boardwalk's end is swept each morning by the toll hands.
Carries the toll box up from the spit at dusk.
Keeps the shelf this wet season because it is her village's turn: sweeps the ash off the stone, sets the salt straight and pulls the burnt offerings back from the water.
Leaves at dusk for Rimfield, the nearest of the villages, up the slope above the pond.
Tends the Hist and clears the fallen leaves from its root each dusk.
Keeps the tribe's ledger of the goods that go down the road to Helstrom.
Holds the spring's ladle on a cord at the stone lip.
Sells beds and rope at the village's agreed price.
Cooks at the fire stand before the hut and keeps the pot covered against the wasps.
Mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell and tests each length for give.
Fills the lodge jars from the spring by noon.
A handful of seed pods rolled on the lodge step; travellers wager a night's meal.
Is bound for Helstrom and pays for the bed in salt.
Has come up from Hissmir to sit with the village's Hist and sleeps in the lodge's guest bed while the tree is heard.
Has charge of the season's crew and sleeps by the stacked cakes.
Works the bellows from first light until the cakes are cool.
Lifts the iron cakes out of the mud and stacks them to dry on the bank.
Draws the water at the well head.
Takes carts across on the plank raft and charges by the wheel.
Keeps the Imperial half's cooking pot apart from the landing's.
Dries fish on the landing racks and calls the well water sour.
A bucket of ford water by the door, topped up at every crossing.
Sits by the brazier at the well with a pack held close.
Pays for a bed and asks every arrival about the road to Gideon.
Keeps the duty roster in the column's pay book.
Steps out from the barricade to ask for the levy and calls it by its Legion name.
Polishes a dented helmet and sets it back in its sack each night.
Cooks at the fire with food bought from the levy.
Hangs each basket's tag on a peg and writes every carriage charge in the book.
Ties off the wrapped bundles for the road home.
Waits in the doorway until the fee is paid.
Lays out the coins for the fee and hands them over with both hands.
Holds the stage office that the family inherited.
Sells the past week's salvage over the stall and reads the ship's name for each lot off its bow-board.
Dries recovered rope in the old stable.
Walks the south shore at low water and drags the wreck timber above the tideline.
Rope-burned palms and a habit of glancing at the second shed.
Wears a silver frill clip and mends salvaged net on the rack.
Stands at the bow of a longboat to call the vote when the council writes.
Mends gear on the deck of the south hull and knows which moorings the tariff men do not pass.
Salt-cracked heels and a bunk below the foredeck.
Hauls cargo from the anchorage to the lighter's hold.
Coils rope on the lighter's deck and drinks Fish-Eye Rye with the nostrils plugged.
Bails the lighter between runs and keeps a jaw beetle in a box for the fights at Archon.
Has untaxed goods to sell off the tradeship and bunks to let below.
Casts off the Lilmoth lighter only on the speaker's nod.
Meets pilgrims where the way meets the water and asks what offering they bring.
Carries the bucket up from the landing.
Has the bell that the pilgrims hear from the landing.
Waist-deep in the shallows through each rite.
Sleeps on a bedroll in the upper rooms.
A long watch on the stair above the pilgrim landing.
Carries the offerings in and leaves each one where it was laid.
Cuts a notched tally stick for every load and hands it over as a receipt.
Stands by the totem at the gate.
Smokes hides over the one fire and keeps the best for trade.
Sleeps in turns in the hide tent.
Flint flakes at the feet from an evening's work by the fire.
Has the bend to watch and whistles when a walker comes into view.
Keeps the shed's fire low and fetches dry reed for the nest from the basket by the door.
Knows every family in the camp and mends the nets at the shed's corner.
Saves the fish heads for the clutch-keeper.
Has the shed names by heart and says them in order after a shift.
Sleeps in the boots under the west shed's thatch.
Patches a sleeping mat with reed from the store.
Carries the day's water up the slope and leaves the first cup at the shed door.
A ledger of debts, open on the lap by the fire.
Walks the yard at dusk and checks each door.
Keeps the offerings at the foot of the Hist filled.
Has the guest stores by the door and houses strangers under the elder's roof.
Has the trade-house key and trades cut cane and smoked fish at the door.
Splits the catch for the smokehouse and turns each fish by hand.
A swept kin-house, ready for whoever comes back from downriver.
Cuts reed and sells it to the dyer by the armful.
Mends nets for the fishers on the rack by the landing.
Dye-stained to the wrist from the vat.
Keeps a jar of trodh by the anvil.
Works the family's lot under the raft and stays down longer than any other diver.
Grades the catch into baskets by size.
Surfaces from the deep lot with the day's shells in a net.
A bone knife and a heap of unopened shells at the grading table.
Has the boats and the lines to mind and never enters the water.
